paragraphs: Here's what this song teaches, friend: faithful people can still hit rock bottom. The psalmist says all this came upon them "though we have not forgotten You or betrayed Your covenant" (Psalm 44:17). Hard times are not always a bill for something you did wrong. If you're in a crushing season and your conscience is clear, this psalm says out loud that you're not the first one standing there.

Now look at what the psalmist does with the pain. He doesn't pretend it's fine, and he doesn't walk away from God. He cries, "Wake up, O Lord! Why are You sleeping? Arise!" (Psalm 44:23). I think that's a person who still believes God is the one who can answer, or he wouldn't bother asking. Honest questions brought to God are not a lack of faith, because the whole song is aimed at Him.

And notice where the song ends. It doesn't tie a bow on the problem. It ends with "Rise up; be our help! Redeem us on account of Your loving devotion" (Psalm 44:26). They ask on account of God's loving devotion, not their own record. So when your own soul feels sunk in the dust, friend, you can hold on, keep talking to God, and lean on His love, not your own strength.
